content:
violet: Heads up — our async ingestion job kept crashing last night due to a JSONDecodeError coming out of the Python SDK when the API returned a non-JSON error payload. The task simply died because we didn't get a structured SDK exception to catch.
omar: ugh. do you have the raw response?
violet: captured:
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Status: 422
Body: validation failed: missing 'account_id'
We call await client.create_event(...) inside an asyncio.create_task and the JSON parsing error escapes.
riley: hmm, the http layer currently calls resp.json() blindly and bubbles JSONDecodeError. Two problems: (1) callers get raw parser exceptions instead of API-level errors; (2) the retry middleware treats any exception as retryable which causes retries on 4xx and duplicates.
patricia: long term we should normalize all non-2xx responses into a single typed exception (RedwoodAPIError) with typed attributes: status_code, error_type (optional), detail/message, raw_body, request_id, and an is_retryable boolean. That makes handling obvious for both sync and async users.
omar: agree. proposal: in the low-level http client do: try: parsed = await resp.json() except Exception as parse_exc: parsed = None; raw = await resp.text(); then if 200 <= resp.status < 300: return parsed if parsed is not None else raw; else: detail = parsed.get('detail') if isinstance(parsed, dict) and 'detail' in parsed else raw; raise RedwoodAPIError(status_code=resp.status, message=detail, raw_body=raw, request_id=resp.headers.get('x-request-id')) from parse_exc
riley: please also set .is_retryable property: default True for >=500, False for 4xx. The retryer should consult getattr(exc, 'is_retryable', None) and only retry if True, otherwise fall back to network-error heuristics.
violet: important for parity: requests.Response.json() sometimes raises ValueError in sync client. Keep the same behavior and ensure sync/async clients produce identical exception types. Also add typed stubs so mypy users can catch RedwoodAPIError and introspect attributes.
patricia: tests we need: plain text 422 -> RedwoodAPIError with raw_body set and is_retryable False; json problem doc -> parsed fields present; xml body -> raw_body fallback or minimal xml->dict parsing optional; 503 -> is_retryable True and gets retried; ensure sync client parity for ValueError path.
omar: small UX note: include a short_message() helper on the exception that returns parsed['detail'] or first 200 chars of raw_body for logs. Also include raw_body always so telemetry can capture unexpected server formats.
riley: I'll draft a small PR: add parse_error helper, RedwoodAPIError class in public API, update retry policy to consult is_retryable, update client stubs, and add unit + async tests.
ci-bot: Created issue #2673: "py-sdk: normalize HTTP error shapes for non-json bodies, add typed exception and tighten retry defaults"
violet: thanks — this should make background tasks resilient and make quickstarts less confusing for new users. :thumbsup:
